sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: for GitHub Actions the subject is built from the entity type, e.g. 'repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:<name>' or 'repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/<branch>', and 'must exactly match the configuration in the GitHub workflow'; no wildcards; issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, audience api://AzureADTokenExchange; at most 20 federated identity credentials per app; an incorrect subject is accepted at creation and fails only at token exchange. The error text is an authored rendering of the sign-in failure (the AADSTS code was not looked up).

brief.situation: You are the DevOps engineer at Corvin Garden Supply. The shop's GitHub Actions workflow deploys to Azure with OpenID Connect: the job runs in GitHub environment 'production' and logs in as the app registration gh-shop-deploy, which trusts that subject. This morning a teammate renamed the environment to 'prod' to match the other repositories. Since then every production deploy fails at azure/login. The spring sale's price release must deploy by 16:30.
handover: Policy: no client secrets for pipelines; federated credentials only.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the workflow's token, its subject claim and the app registration's federated credentials.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why login failed, what you changed, and why not a client secret.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The token's subject became repo:corvin/shop:environment:prod after the 10:05 rename; gh-shop-deploy trusted only ...:environment:production, and federated credentials match subjects exactly.

parts.label: Changed
parts.criteria: New exact trust, stale one removed.
parts.modelAnswer: Added a federated credential for ...:environment:prod (the environment kept its reviewers and branch policy) and deleted the old one; the deploy logged in with OIDC.

parts.label: No secret
parts.modelAnswer: A client secret would have been a long-lived credential in GitHub, against policy and the reason for OIDC. The credential is now in code, and CI checks environment names against it.

expertPath.text: Subject environment:prod; app trusts environment:production; renamed at 10:05; protections intact.
Add the prod credential, delete the stale one, re-run; code and CI check.

secretStored.headline: Keep it secretless
secretStored.body: The trust was broken by a name, not by the design. Add a federated credential for the new subject; a stored secret is what workload identity federation exists to avoid.

pricesStale.headline: The subject must match exactly
pricesStale.body: A federated credential trusts one exact subject. Renaming the environment changed the subject; the app needs a credential for the new one.

trusted.headline: Good: fixed the trust, not the policy
trusted.body: You read the subject in the error, compared it with the app's credentials, traced the rename, added the exact new subject and removed the old one, verified the deploy, and tied future renames to the trust.

scoring.modelReasoning: The login error shows the token's subject is environment:prod, and the app's federated credential still names environment:production; subjects must match exactly. Add a credential for the new subject (the renamed environment kept its protections), remove the stale one, and re-run. A client secret works only by bringing back the long-lived credential OIDC removed; a plain re-run changes nothing. Manage the credentials in code and check names in CI.
